55.title: Installing the Breed bootloader
55.titles: Linksys EA7XXX › Installing from stock firmware
55.text: Installing OpenWrt Install OpenWrt for your device as described on the official website. Saving the calibration Save EEPROM/factory/mtd2 from your device. Installing the package Give the router internet access and install the kmod-mtd-rw package. Writing the bootloader Open a console and connect to the router over SSH. Serve breed.bin with HFS and run the commands: Enter one command at a time 1 cd /tmp 2 wget http://192.168.1.2/breed.bin 3 insmod mtd-rw i_want_a_brick= 1 4 mtd unlock /dev/mtd0 5 mtd write /tmp/breed.bin boot 6 reboot Backup Open Breed at 192.168.1.1 and save a Full backup in case you want to return to the factory firmware.

56.title: Flashing through Breed
56.titles: Linksys EA7XXX › Installing from stock firmware
56.text: Serving the files Start HFS and put all files from the archive into it, along with your calibration (EEPROM/factory/mtd2 ). The correct MAC addresses must be written into the calibration beforehand with the EEPROM tools. Flashing over Telnet Start PuTTY, connect over Telnet to 192.168.1.1 on port 23 and paste the commands with the right mouse button, waiting for the previous one to finish. Warning Turn off your OS firewall and antivirus beforehand. The messages skipped bad blocks and Flash erasure failed with -5 after entering the commands are normal. Caution Each line is a separate command. If it fails, run it again. Compare the IP in the wget commands below with the IP shown in HFS. In the Breed bootloader it always starts with 192.168.1.xxx. Enter one command at a time 1 flash erase 0x80000 0x7f00000 2 wget http://192.168.1.2/u-config.bin 3 flash write 0x80000 0x80001000 0x80000 4 flash write 0x4040000 0x80001000 0x80000 5 wget http://192.168.1.2/eeprom.bin 6 flash write 0x100000 0x80001000 0x80000 7 flash write 0x40c0000 0x80001000 0x80000 8 wget http://192.168.1.2/firmware.bin 9 flash write 0x180000 0x80001000 0x1AB3F00 10 flash write 0x4140000 0x80001000 0x1AB3F00 11 wget http://192.168.1.2/u-state.bin 12 flash write 0x3fc0000 0x80001000 0x80000 13 env set autoboot.command " boot flash 0x4140000 " 14 env save 15 reset Sample console output After the reboot the device starts Done! Router access Web interface 192.168.1.1 Wi-Fi password 12345678

299.text: Hold the Reset button for 10–15 seconds while the system is running, or reset through the web interface. 2

300.text: You cannot: every build already contains the largest available set. The memory layout differs between models, so it is impossible to add all components. Viewing the installed components from the system is not available. 3

301.title: There is no USB port speed switch
301.text: On models with USB 3.0 the switch may be missing from the web interface. 302.title: How do I add a device to Mesh?
302.text: Switch the device to repeater mode following the official guide, then capture it. Tip Mesh can be set up both with original routers and with clones. Make sure the devices have different service data — Mesh capture requires it. It is better to capture flashed devices over a cable. After a successful capture you can unplug it: the connection switches to Wi-Fi. If you run into problems, see the troubleshooting section. 5

303.title: Can I update with the official firmware?
303.text: No. A self-update may overwrite the bootloader, and the device will no longer start. Recovery will then require UART or a programmer. 6

304.title: The official bootloader is installed
304.text: Info If the official bootloader is installed and cannot be replaced the usual way: Download the NAND Breed rewrite file. In the running system, upload it as an update. After the reboot, enter Breed and upload the required files following the guide for your model. Tip If the router has no room for Entware or does not start, connect via TFTPD64 / UART and replace the bootloader. Tip On SmartBox Flash the stock bootloader expects the file name KN-1810_recovery.bin for TFTPD64 7

305.title: The system does not boot past Breed
305.text: Enter this command in Telnet: abstatus a) Autoboot command has been successfully executed / Firmware boot failed. The firmware was not written correctly. On devices with NAND memory use method #3. b) Autoboot was interrupted by button press. The Reset button was held during power-on. If nobody pressed it, roll back to another Breed version or use the version for another device. 312.title: Glossary
312.text: Short explanations of words used in the guides. In the guides these words are underlined with dots — hover over them or tap them to see the explanation.

314.title: Breed
314.text: An alternative bootloader for routers with Broadcom and MediaTek processors. Its web interface or Telnet console is used to write the firmware, EEPROM and other partitions. More about Breed K

315.title: KeenBOOT
315.text: A proprietary bootloader for routers based on MediaTek MT7621 and MT7981 with a web interface: firmware installation, full dump, backups. More about KeenBOOT

317.title: EEPROM
317.text: A flash memory partition with the Wi-Fi calibration and the MAC address. Every router has its own: without the right EEPROM, Wi-Fi works poorly or not at all. You can extract it from a dump and set the MAC in the tools. U

318.title: U-Config
318.text: A partition with the device's service data: serial number, service tag, service password and region. A new U-Config can be generated in the tools. F

319.title: Full dump
319.text: A complete backup of the router's entire flash memory. With it, the device can be returned to its original state. O

320.title: OTA
320.text: An over-the-air update: the new version is downloaded and installed right on the router, without files on a computer. O

321.title: OpenWrt
321.text: An open Linux-based firmware for routers. On some models our firmware is installed from it.

323.title: KeenKit
323.text: A router maintenance script: firmware updates from a file and over OTA, partition and Entware backups. More about KeenKit E

324.title: Entware
324.text: A repository of extra software for the router. It is installed with the opkg package manager to the built-in memory or a USB drive. Installing Entware M

325.title: Mesh
325.text: Several routers combined into one Wi-Fi network with shared management. Mesh setup

327.title: BreedEnter
327.text: A Windows program that interrupts the system boot and opens the Breed bootloader without the Reset button. How to use it H

328.title: HFS
328.text: HTTP File Server — a simple Windows program that shares files over the network. Breed downloads firmware files from it with the wget command. P

329.title: PuTTY
329.text: A Windows program for connecting to the router's console over Telnet or SSH. T

330.title: TFTPD64
330.text: A TFTP server program for Windows. Some factory bootloaders download the firmware file through it during recovery.

332.title: Telnet
332.text: A text console protocol. It is used to enter commands in the Breed bootloader — strictly one at a time. S

333.title: SSH
333.text: A secure connection to the router's console: for example, to install Entware or run KeenKit. U

334.title: UART
334.text: A serial port on the router's board. With a USB-UART adapter you can control the bootloader even when the system does not start.

335.title: KeenBOOT
335.text: A proprietary bootloader for MediaTek MT7621 and MT7981. Advantages Improved bad block handling Web interface with file uploads Upload of a full device dump DHCP support without setting a static IP address Stopping the system boot with BreedEnter Dual-Image support for mipsel

342.text: Caution Do not update the bootloader if everything works. Go to the Update section, choose the KeenBOOT (U-Boot) target partition, select the bootloader file and click Update.

343.title: KeenKit
343.text: A multi-purpose script that makes router maintenance easier. What the script can do Update firmware from file Finds a .bin file on the built-in or an external drive and installs it to the Firmware partitions. Partition backup Saves the selected partitions to the chosen drive. Entware backup Creates a full backup of the drive the script runs from. You can use it for a new installation. Replace partition Replaces a system partition with a file chosen by the user. OTA Update Online upgrade or downgrade of the firmware. Update service data Creates a new U-Config with updated service data and replaces the current one. KeenBOOT OTA Update Online upgrade or downgrade of the bootloader.

344.title: Installation
344.text: Install Entware. Connect to the router over SSH. Run the command: opkg update && opkg install curl && curl -L -s " https://raw.githubusercontent.com/spatiumstas/KeenKit/main/install.sh " > /tmp/install.sh && sh /tmp/install.sh Alternative source: opkg update && opkg install curl && curl -L -s " https://raw.githubusercontent.com/project-athens-dev/osvault/main/scripts/install.sh " > /tmp/install.sh && sh /tmp/install.sh

347.title: Adding a node over cable
347.text: In System settings, click Change operating mode and set the additional internet center mode Extender/Repeater. Connect the router to the controller with a cable. Caution! Since version 5.0.1, a device switched to Repeater mode may keep its login password. Remove it or reset the settings: Open the repeater's web interface. Remove the password through the CLI: user admin no pass Run the command on the controller. candidate is the repeater's MAC address; press Tab to fill it in automatically: mws revisit {candidate} Click Capture. Transferring the settings may take up to 2 minutes. When the capture succeeds, the router appears in the list with its serial number in the name, for example: Keenetic N6 AX1800 037***462.

348.title: Adding a node wirelessly
348.text: In System settings (General settings), click Change operating mode and set the additional internet center mode Extender/Repeater. After the mode changes, connect to the router with a cable or over Wi-Fi. The web interface will be available at 192.168.1.3. To connect with a cable, set a static IP address on the network card. In the Wireless ISP section, connect to the controller's wireless network. Caution! Since version 5.0.1, a device switched to Repeater mode may keep its login password. Remove it or reset the settings: Open the repeater's web interface. Remove the password through the CLI: user admin no pass Run the command on the controller. candidate is the repeater's MAC address; press Tab to fill it in automatically: mws revisit {candidate} Capture the node on the controller. Transferring the settings may take up to 2 minutes. When the capture succeeds, the router appears in the list with its serial number in the name, for example: Keenetic N6 AX1800 037***462.

350.title: 1. The node is not captured
350.titles: Setting up a Mesh system › Troubleshooting
350.text: Make sure the devices you add have different serial numbers. It is shown on the home page in the About system block. If the serial numbers match, use the U-Config generator or KeenKit with the Replace service data function. Using the U-Config generator: Open the U-Config tab Drag the U-Config from the firmware archive into the upload area or choose the file in the dialog. Download the generated file and flash it, or replace it with KeenKit. On devices with SPI memory you can load a full dump (Full) saved in Breed into the script and restore from it.

351.title: 2. Does not connect over the air after a wired capture
351.titles: Setting up a Mesh system › Troubleshooting
351.text: Enable Wireless backhaul on the controller.

352.title: 3. Error Mws::Controller::Candidate: "xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx": invalid CSR response
352.titles: Setting up a Mesh system › Troubleshooting
352.text: The error appears after capturing a device with the same service number and/or MAC address. To fix it, follow the steps from the first item.

353.title: 4. Error failed to connect: operation timeout
353.titles: Setting up a Mesh system › Troubleshooting
353.text: This is a normal message: the repeater is trying to reach the servers. It does not affect Mesh.

355.title: MediaTek MT7981 SPI NAND Flash
355.text: If you do not have a full 128 MB backup, merge the factory partitions with Merger or run this command in a terminal: copy /b mtd0.bin+mtd1.bin+mtd2.bin+mtd8.bin+mtd5.bin+mtd6.bin+mtd7.bin full_dump.bin For Xiaomi AX3000T the file will be 5.6 MB: it contains all partitions needed before flashing. Enter the KeenBOOT bootloader. In the Update section, upload the backup file as Full image (Single Image). Warning On Xiaomi AX3000T, restore the device with the MiWiFi Repair Tool after the restart.

356.title: MediaTek MT7622 SPI NAND Flash
356.text: Using the files and steps from the recovery instructions, put the OpenWrt image into the folder, renaming the files to AX6S_recovery.bin and KN-1811_recovery.bin beforehand. After OpenWrt starts, upload the factory backups and write them to the flash memory. Commands Enter one command at a time 1 opkg update 2 opkg install kmod-mtd-rw 3 insmod mtd-rw i_want_a_brick= 1 4 cd /tmp/ 5 mtd unlock /dev/mtd2 6 mtd write /tmp/mtd3_uboot.bin u-boot 7 mtd unlock /dev/mtd3 8 mtd write /tmp/mtd4_Nvram.bin u-boot-env 9 mtd unlock /dev/mtd4 10 mtd write /tmp/mtd5_Bdata.bin bdata 11 mtd unlock /dev/mtd5 12 mtd write /tmp/mtd6_Factory.bin factory After the device reboots, use MIWIFIRepairTool to install the factory firmware.

358.title: Method I NAND Flash
358.text: Install KeenBOOT version 1.4 or later. In the Update section, upload the backup file as Full image (Single Image). Upload the device backup. Caution! The full device backup must be exactly 128 MB (134,217,728 bytes). Tip If the router boots into Breed after the restore, install the factory bootloader for your model (see step 7 below). Archive of stock MT7621 bootloaders

359.title: Method II NAND Flash
359.text: Open the backup in HxD. Select the first block that contains the Breed bootloader and delete it. Save the resulting file. It must be exactly 127 MB (133,693,440 bytes). Enter the Breed bootloader (how?) at 192.168.1.1. Add the backup to HFS. In PuTTY, run the commands that erase the memory and write the backup. Enter one command at a time 1 wget http://192.168.1.2/full.bin 2 flash erase 0x80000 0x7f00000 3 flash write 0x80000 0x80001000 0x7f80000 Go to the Upgrade section, choose the factory bootloader file in the Bootloader field and click Upload.

360.title: Method III SPI NOR
360.text: Enter the Breed bootloader (how?) at 192.168.1.1. Upload a 16 or 32 MB backup, depending on the device's memory size. Go to the Upgrade section, choose the factory bootloader file in the Bootloader field and click Upload.

361.title: Tools
361.text: Everything runs locally in your browser: files are not uploaded anywhere. α Set MAC Write the router's MAC address into an EEPROM file β EEPROM Mover Copy a calibration block to another offset γ Extract EEPROM Find the EEPROM in a full flash dump δ U-Config New unique service data for U-Config α Set MAC address Writes your MAC address into a MediaTek EEPROM (factory) file. The finished file downloads right away. 1 Enter the router's MAC address Both AABBCCDDEEFF and AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF work. 2 Choose the EEPROM file Drop the EEPROM file here or click to choose a file .bin

362.title: Updating firmware
362.text: Info You can also download the update file manually.

363.title: Official
363.text: For 5.0.7 and later Open System settings. Upload the update file to the firmware field. Confirm the update. The device will reboot.

365.title: Method I Recommended
365.text: Enter the KeenBOOT bootloader. Upload the update file through the web interface.

366.title: Method II Automatic
366.text: Use KeenKit with the Update firmware from file or OTA Update function.

367.title: Method III Via Breed
367.text: Caution A mistake in the commands may leave the router inoperable. Follow the instructions carefully. Enter Breed. Start PuTTY and connect over Telnet to 192.168.1.1 on port 23. Paste the commands one at a time with the right mouse button, waiting for each one to finish. Serve the firmware file with HFS.exe, for example under the name firmware.bin. Commands for devices with 256MB flash storage (SmartBox Pro, Xiaomi R3P) Run the commands one at a time, waiting for the previous one to finish. Enter one command at a time 1 flash erase 0x180000 0x1AB3F00 2 flash erase 0x8140000 0x1AB3F00 3 wget http://192.168.1.2/firmware.bin 4 flash write 0x180000 0x80001000 0x1AB3F00 5 flash write 0x8140000 0x80001000 0x1AB3F00 6 reset Commands for other devices Run the commands one at a time, waiting for the previous one to finish. Enter one command at a time 1 flash erase 0x180000 0x1AB3F00 2 flash erase 0x4140000 0x1AB3F00 3 wget http://192.168.1.2/firmware.bin 4 flash write 0x180000 0x80001000 0x1AB3F00 5 flash write 0x4140000 0x80001000 0x1AB3F00 6 reset

368.title: SPI NOR memory (up to 32MB)
368.text: Enter Breed. Open Upgrade → Generic → Firmware, choose the firmware file and upload it. The section names may differ depending on the Breed version. Note This section is for the firmware file only. Do not upload a full dump to it. After a successful upload the router reboots into the system.

369.title: Wiki
369.text: Ported firmware provides the basic functionality and supports most features of the original system, except for the vendor's cloud services. For evaluation only Ported firmware is an unofficial build. It is meant only for getting to know the system, not for everyday use. Do not use it on the listed routers as your main solution and do not install it on a device your internet connection or work depends on: failures, loss of settings and a bricked router are possible. All firmware, scripts and other files are provided “as is”, without warranty or technical support. Caution! Do not use the original firmware update files: this may leave the device inoperable. Do not contact official support or its chats about ported firmware. Doing so may get you banned from our chats. You bear full responsibility for the risks of flashing your device yourself. You can explore the range of original Keenetic products and find out where to buy them on the official website. Choose your model in the “Firmware” section of the side menu: each device page has the specifications, build features and a step-by-step installation guide.
